title: Microsoft 365 admin center: usage insights for Copilot Chat pay-as-you-go billing
summary: Hold: disconnecting a billing policy is not the only documented way to prevent metered agent use; Microsoft also documents blocking agents. The briefing also treats the newer Cost Management dashboard as a Copilot Chat monitoring surface without establishing that coverage. The roadmap facts, published message-meter rate and budget warning are supported.

claims.claim: The underlying Copilot Chat pay-as-you-go agent usage has a consumption licensing model and is billed to the configured Azure subscription through an Azure meter.

claims.fix: Retain the underlying consumption model, but add to the licensing notes: 'The Copilot-node setup page also requires the tenant to have at least one SharePoint licence, or a licence that includes SharePoint.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/commerce/services/pay-as-you-go-setup-copilot. This requirement appears on that cited setup page but not on the other setup page summarised in Scope.

To give the disconnect control named in the note, use 'Copilot > Cost management > Classic Billing & usage > Pay-as-you-go services > Microsoft Copilot Chat > Connected', set docs to https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/commerce/services/pay-as-you-go-setup-copilot, and say that the Connected toggle is turned off in Manage billing policy connections. claims.claim: The billing-policy connection toggle is the only documented control that ends metered use.
claims.quote: You can enable, disable, assign, block, or remove agents for your organization ... Members of your organization can only access the agents that you have allowed.
